memory_candidates.content: Bash pitfall: `"${var:-{}}"` (using a literal `{}` as a parameter-expansion default) does NOT do what it looks like. Bash's `${var:-word}` default-word matching stops at the FIRST unescaped `}`, so on a non-empty `$var` it silently appends a stray trailing `}` after the expansion, corrupting downstream JSON and making a piped `jq ... 2>/dev/null` call fail closed to empty/default rather than erroring loudly. Safe replacement: `[ -z "${var:-}" ] && var='{}'` as a separate guard statement before use. This is easy to miss with `bash -n` (pure syntax check) — it requires a functional simulation with a non-empty value to catch.

When adding or testing a new skill_-prefixed function in scripts/skill-base.sh, override SKILL_REPO_ROOT to a temp fixture directory before sourcing the file (`export SKILL_REPO_ROOT="$TMP"; source scripts/skill-base.sh`). Every skill_ write function resolves its state.json path relative to SKILL_REPO_ROOT (not a hardcoded 'specs/state.json'), so this lets you exercise real read-modify-write logic — including adversarial-string round-tripping — against a disposable fixture repo without ever touching the real repo's specs/state.json. Confirm via `stat -c %Y` before/after that the real file's mtime is unchanged.
